questions.stem: Which three types of storage exist at the hardware level?
options: Object Storage, File Storage and Block Storage
Row Storage, Columnar Storage and In-Memory Storage
Data Warehouse, Data Lake and Data Lakehouse
Key-Value, Document and Graph Storage
Physical, Virtual and Cloud Storage
questions.explanation: There are three types of storage at the hardware level: Object Storage, File Storage and Block Storage.

questions.stem: How does Object Storage organise data?
options: In folders and subfolders arranged in a hierarchy
In a flat open storage area with no folders or subfolders, each object kept with its metadata and a unique identifier
As fixed-size blocks each with a unique address
As rows and columns inside tables
As nodes connected by edges
questions.explanation: Object Storage considers all types of data as an object. Data is stored in a flat open storage area with no folder or subfolder concept, along with its metadata and unique identifier, forming a storage pool that keeps all details about the data near to it.

questions.stem: Which everyday analogy is used to describe File Storage?
options: Parcels in a postal sorting office
Books on a library shelf
Keeping manual papers in files during school days
Cards in a card index
Rooms in a hotel
questions.explanation: File Storage is compared with how manual papers were kept in files in school days: data is kept inside folders and subfolders in a hierarchy, and to find data you need to know the folder's location or path.

questions.stem: What do you need to know in order to retrieve specific data from File Storage?
options: The object's unique identifier
The block's unique address
The name of the cloud provider
The location or path of the folder
The metadata stored beside the object
questions.explanation: In File Storage, data sits inside folders and subfolders, so when you need specific data you just need to know the location or path of the folder.

questions.stem: How does Block Storage treat a file?
options: As a single object with attached metadata
As a document with data type descriptions
As a row in a table
As an entry in a folder hierarchy
As a single block of data, with each block stored as a separate piece of information and given a unique address
questions.explanation: Block Storage considers a file as a single block of data, and each block is stored as a separate piece of information with a unique address for reference.

questions.stem: Which systems are named as being stored in blocks at the backend?
options: Traditional databases and Hadoop files
AWS S3 and Azure ADLS
Data Lakes and Delta Lakes
Shared drives and Data Rooms
Spreadsheets and email archives
questions.explanation: Traditional databases are stored in blocks, and at the backend Hadoop files are also stored in blocks.

questions.stem: Which storage type have cloud companies adopted as their de facto storage in the era of big data, data lakes, delta lakes and data lakehouses?
options: Block Storage
Object Storage
File Storage
Tape Storage
In-Memory Storage
questions.explanation: In the era of big data, data lake, delta lake and data lakehouse, cloud companies use Object Storage as their de facto storage, for example S3 on AWS and ADLS on Azure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Object Storage?
options: All types of data are treated as objects
Each object is stored with its metadata
Objects are arranged in folders and subfolders
Each object has a unique identifier
Data lives in a flat open storage area
questions.explanation: Object Storage has no folder or subfolder concept; folders and subfolders in a hierarchy are the hallmark of File Storage.

questions.stem: Which are given as examples of Object Storage offered by cloud companies?
options: HDFS and EXT
MySQL and SQL Server
Hive and Cosmos DB
S3 on AWS and ADLS on Azure
FAT and NTFS
questions.explanation: Cloud examples of Object Storage are S3 (AWS) and ADLS (Azure); Teradata and Oracle also call it Object Storage.

questions.stem: What distinguishes File Storage from Object Storage in the way data is organised?
options: File Storage stores metadata beside each item, whereas Object Storage stores none
File Storage assigns a unique address to each block, whereas Object Storage uses folders
File Storage is used only in the cloud, whereas Object Storage is used only on-premises
File Storage treats every file as an object, whereas Object Storage treats every object as a file
File Storage keeps data in a hierarchy of folders and subfolders, whereas Object Storage uses a flat storage area
questions.explanation: File Storage keeps data as one piece of information inside folders and subfolders, in a hierarchy mode, in contrast with Object Storage's flat open storage area with no folder concept.
